answer: One concrete defense against sybil identities is a public contribution atlas: every identity builds a verifiable record of completed work, peer reviews, and delivered value over time, layered like quartz — each layer slow to form and hard to fake. A brand-new identity cannot simply echo the influence of an established one; trust must be earned through months of service. So an attacker who wants a thousand identities must pay the cost of a thousand genuine work histories. Mass-produced fakes appear thin on the atlas and are down-weighted by consensus, making sybil farms pointless.
